rows.method: Hardware trigger: Arduino-driven FSIN (InnoMaker OV9281, CT_FOCUS_AUTO trigger mode, MoCapSTR-style sync box)
rows.stack: ATmega328P Timer1 pulses to camera FSIN opto input; trigger mode switched via UVC CT_FOCUS_AUTO through OpenCV DSHOW / V4L2 (planned)
rows.platform: Windows DSHOW + Linux V4L2 (plan v1); macOS out of scope

sync.value: Designed to align exposure starts; skew/lockout unmeasured (plan only)
sync.note: One electrical edge drives every camera's FSIN, so oscillator error is common-mode; this is the only approach in the research that controls when light is integrated rather than timestamping it. Unknowns: FSIN-edge-to-exposure skew per camera ('up to ~1 ms' plan estimate, possibly gated by bridge firmware; no vendor/third-party figure found); ~18-20 ms re-trigger lockout (MoCapSTR's own sweeps, not reproduced) caps ~50 fps; a +0.5% resonator at nominal 50 Hz could make cameras reject different pulses (hence 48 Hz default). OV9281 is global shutter. Needs trigger-capable cameras: C922/C930e/generic have no FSIN. Planned M0 spike: 0-25 ms delayed 50 us flash sweep per camera.

timestamp.value: Frame = pulse index; host-fitted rate; edge latency unmeasured
timestamp.note: Plan assigns pulse index from frame intervals with a 10 s sliding rate fit plus a firmware pulse counter; edges are cycle-exact (62.5 ns) on the Arduino clock, which is not the host clock (resonator +-0.5%, rate fitted on host from perf_counter frame stamps). Absolute exposure time = edge + unmeasured FSIN latency; host mapping still rests on arrival times (CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC on V4L2).

mjpeg.value: Orthogonal; plan captures via OpenCV, which decodes
mjpeg.note: Trigger is independent of the capture API; a passthrough stack (MF/PyAV/V4L2) could be paired with it but that is untested, and the trigger switch relies on a UVC control write through the same stack.

unique_id.value: Orthogonal; camera ID comes from the capture stack

bandwidth.value: No effect on USB alt; capture stack decides

exposure.note: Set through the capture stack (OpenCV in plan). On Linux the vendor order is auto_exposure=1 before focus_automatic_continuous=1.

format.value: Rate set by pulses, <= ~50 fps (MoCapSTR lockout); fps fixed at open

The UVC autofocus control is consumed as the trigger-mode switch; a camera left in trigger mode looks dead, so the plan reverts it in finally.

sync.value: No: free-running UVC; no trigger or start alignment
sync.note: No API in OpenCV or DirectShow starts or triggers an exposure (SURVEY: no surveyed project controls exposure start on generic UVC webcams). No cross-camera timing was measured on this path. Measured DSHOW-cell rates: C922 30.00, C930e 30.04, generic 25.77 fps. Derived from those: the C922-C930e phase walks about 1.3 ms/s, a full frame every ~25 s (the extractor's 1.7 ms/s used the MF rate of 30.05).

timestamp.value: None: POS_MSEC = -1; only host time after read()
timestamp.note: pos_msec is -1.0 on all 367 C922 frames, so the only time is a host clock read after read()/decode. DSHOW arrival was never scored against the flash ground truth. For comparison, MF-path host arrival scored 4.6-5.0 ms on the C922 (REPORT finding 7, on the 16 ms grid; the flash method floor is ~0.5 ms). capture_backends_review says OpenCV uses the preview pin, which has no timestamps (inferred/web).

mjpeg.value: No: always BGR; 24.6-39.6% of a core
mjpeg.note: CONVERT_RGB=0 still returns BGR with the size-first order, or YUY2 at ~10 fps with the fourcc-first order. No JPEG bytes come back in either order.

DShow indices changed (C930e 7->2). The check that cv2.VideoCapture(index) opens the expected physical camera was skipped because of the Kiyo risk.

bandwidth.note: In both all-3 cells the generic camera, which shares a hub with the C930e, failed to open (index 1: open failed). The max-alt choice (32/32) was measured on MF; that DS uses the same usbvideo grant is inferred. DirectShow has no alt-setting knob (SURVEY).

exposure.value: Only via separate DS IAMCameraControl; CAP_PROP_EXPOSURE untested
exposure.note: Exposure was set before each cell by a separate process (mf_mjpeg_capture --controls-only --via-dshow: IAMCameraControl/IKsControl on the DS filter). The C922 and generic read back -7 manual after the capture; the C930e read back -5, the most it accepts via that path. In the all-3 cells the generic camera, which failed to open, read back exposure flagged auto. Only the readback was checked, not the effect. OpenCV's own CAP_PROP_EXPOSURE was never tested. C930e manual exposure is unreliable on every API.

The generic camera has no focus control. expected: settable through the same DS IAMCameraControl side channel; OpenCV CAP_PROP_FOCUS/AUTOFOCUS untested.

sync.note: MF has no trigger or start control (inferred), and the measured rates differ (30.00 / 30.05 / 25.76 fps), so exposures are not aligned. Derived: the C922-C930e phase walks one frame every ~20 s. Measuring offsets is not established either. The 0.064 ms GT-offset agreement (CI95 -0.11 to 0.26) reflects where the ROIs fall, not sync accuracy: the offset moves 35 ms across image blocks. Online mapping gives -0.30 or +4.1 ms (VERIFY section 6). Finding 15, provisional: C930e (libusb SCR) minus C922 (MF PTS) had a std of 0.54-0.79 ms over 5 runs. PTS rate vs ground truth: +35 ppm (C930e), -3.9 ppm (C922). No run was longer than 30 s.

timestamp.value: C922 UVC PTS <=~0.5 ms (method floor); OS 4.4 ms; admin
timestamp.note: C922 uvc_pts_mapped_direct: 0.47-0.68 ms std vs flash ground truth over six -7 runs, and 0.40 ms in one -9 run. That is the method floor (~0.5 ms): a frame counter scores the same, and in some runs the GT is built from the same PTS source (gt_ref). The best scores use a whole-run (non-causal) fit; causal fits give 0.59-1.13 ms. C922 PTS sits near the end of exposure (offset -1.14 x exposure change), and rolling shutter spans ~30-31 ms per frame, so the per-row offset to light hitting the sensor needs calibration. C930e PTS is synthetic: use SCR, though its exposure was uncertain. OS sample time (= llTimestamp = DeviceTimestamp) is on a 16 ms grid and scored 4.40-4.52 ms. Metadata needs the MetadataBufferSizeInKB0 registry value (admin) plus a replug per camera. The generic camera was never enabled, so its timing is unmeasured.

mjpeg.value: Yes: camera's own bytes, 100% valid (lenient), 0.7-2.2% core
mjpeg.note: The output subtype stays MJPG, so no decoder MFT is in the reader. Generic 1080p frames pass only a lenient decode; strict libjpeg-turbo fails on every frame. Frame Server CPU was excluded because it needs elevation.

unique_id.note: The MF symbolic link embeds the function instance ID. api_names.json resolves it to the composite ID (serial B76395EF on the C922, hub/port otherwise) and LocationPaths. After the C930e WinUSB rollback the symlink changed but the serial/port key did not. Opening by symlink touches only the matched camera. The naming harness passed 46/46 claim checks overall (not MF-specific). The controlled reboot/replug/port-move test has not run.

bandwidth.note: Max-alt reservations are ~24.5 MB/s each (~62% of the USB 2.0 periodic budget), so effectively one MJPEG camera per USB 2.0 link. The refusal shows only at the first ReadSample. No surveyed library has an MF bandwidth knob.

exposure.note: mf_uvc_timing sets exposure through IAMCameraControl queried from the IMFMediaSource before streaming. C922: readback -9/-7/-6 with luma 24/65/95, and the fixed-ROI PTS offset tracks exposure, so the setting was applied. Generic: -7 is its range minimum. C930e: reads back -7 but integrated about a full frame in 4 of 5 valid runs. Cause open (control set before stream start does not stick; LogiTune not excluded). Re-applying after stream start was never tested. The MJPEG-matrix MF cells used the DS-filter side channel and do not demonstrate MF control.

sync.value: No: free-running cameras; barrier aligns stream start only
sync.note: main.rs waits on a std::sync::Barrier before open_stream(). That aligns the API calls, not exposures. No cross-camera exposure alignment was ever measured through nokhwa. The only cross-camera figure (REPORT finding 15, provisional: 0.54-0.79 ms std of the C930e libusb SCR minus C922 MF PTS offset) used other stacks. Clocks drift: C930e STC +42.3 to +49.5 ppm vs QPC between sessions (docs/usb_camera_report.md). Against ground truth the PTS rates were +35 ppm (C930e) and -3.9 ppm (C922) (VERIFY_method.md). So the phase walks about 39 us/s, a full frame in about 14 min (derived). That was measured on MF metadata and libusb, not nokhwa.

timestamp.value: MF sample time on 16 ms grid; no UVC PTS exposed
timestamp.note: capture_timestamp is the MF IMFSample time (QPC domain). Intervals are 32/48 ms (p50 32.0, p99 48.0). Host minus sample time is bimodal: ~0.3 ms and ~16 ms modes on the C922/C930e, 16/32 ms modes on the generic camera (lat_grid_now.txt). The flash score is transferred, not direct: the same MF sample time scored 4.40-4.52 ms std vs flash on the C922 (finding 7). It was never scored through nokhwa. No path to MFSampleExtension_CaptureMetadata (inferred: Buffer carries only capture_timestamp).

mjpeg.value: Yes: 593/593, 588/588, 515/515 frames valid JPEG (SOI/EOI)
mjpeg.note: These counts come from the three single-camera runs. In the all-3 run the generic camera got 0 frames (bandwidth refusal). Validity is SOI/EOI on every frame plus a decode of 20 samples. No header-hash comparison against MF was made, so 'not re-encoded' is inferred from the MF native-type request. Needs RequestedFormatType::Exact MJPEG, because compatible_camera_formats() keeps at most 2 FourCCs and hides MJPEG on the Logitech cameras.

unique_id.value: misc() = MF symbolic link; maps to camera_key; opens by index
unique_id.note: The symlink matches naming's msmf_symbolic_link (ks_video_camera_symlink), so it can be looked up to the serial/port key. The symlink itself is not stable: the C930e's changed &0& -> &1& between the 10-25 and 10-28 runs, after the WinUSB rollback (finding 23). Capture opens by CameraIndex::Index, which is unstable. Opening by symlink was never tested. Listing opens every camera.

bandwidth.value: No alt control; refusal surfaces as 0x800718CF read errors
bandwidth.note: 'No bandwidth knob' comes from source/docs (SURVEY). Measured side effect: in the all-3 run the generic camera got 0 frames with 'Could not capture frame ... desired bandwidth (0x800718CF)', and read_errors reached 17,387,202, a hot error loop. nokhwa_probe cannot stagger or record start order.

exposure.value: nokhwa reads back only; manual set needs side-channel IAMCameraControl
exposure.note: Source only: nokhwa's set_control reuses the current auto/manual flag, so it cannot switch auto to manual (nokhwa-bindings-windows 0.4.6). The probe set -7 through IAMCameraControl, QI'd from a separately activated MF media source. nokhwa's camera_control() then read back Manual -7. The C922 and generic read back -7 after capture. The C930e read back -5 after every capture (RERUN: weakened), consistent with finding 11. Whether the exposure was actually integrated was not checked against the flash through nokhwa.

format.value: Exact 1280x720@30 MJPEG works; format list hides MJPEG
format.note: Delivered 29.996/30.06 fps for a requested 30 (generic 25.74, its real rate). camera_format() reports '1280x720@1 MJPEG', a wrong fps readback. The format list keeps at most 2 FourCCs, drops H264 and zeroes non-integer rates.

focus.note: The probe touched only Exposure, WhiteBalance and Gain. expected: KnownCameraControl::Focus exists, with the same auto->manual flag limitation, so it would need the same IAMCameraControl side channel.

rows.costs: Rust crate, no Python package (needs a PyO3 binding). Depends on Frame Server. Listing opens every camera. Manual exposure needs extra Windows COM code. Bandwidth refusal becomes a busy error loop.
rows.verdict: Native MJPEG works, but identity, controls and timestamps add nothing over raw MF; not worth the dependency.

sync.value: No: free-running; C930e−C922 offset varies 0.54–0.79 ms run-to-run
sync.note: Standard UVC streaming has no frame-start trigger, so libusb can only timestamp exposures, not align them. The 0.54–0.79 ms figure is the std across 5 runs of the per-run C930e (libusb SCR) minus C922 (MF PTS, a different API) offset at fixed image rows, i.e. at the flash-method floor (REPORT finding 15, provisional); it is not an alignment. Drift: C930e STC +42.3 to +44.7 ppm vs QPC in runs 2–6 (doc: +42.3 to +49.5 across sessions); must be refitted per session. Computed: ~42 ppm walks one 33 ms frame in ~13 min against a nominal-rate clock. Relative drift between two cameras was not measured. Only a hardware trigger (FSIN) could align exposures (arduino_sync is a plan; nothing built).

timestamp.value: SCR 0.41–0.74 ms MAD (method floor); IOCTL basis weakened
timestamp.note: Runs 2–6 (C930e exposure re-applied after start): SCR→QPC 0.41–0.74 ms MAD vs flash ground truth; back-dated first-payload arrival 0.39–0.78 ms; pure frame-counter model 0.36–0.73 ms, so the true accuracy is an upper bound of ~0.5 ms (method floor). Raw libusb host arrival 1.0–1.7 ms MAD vs 5.8–6.1 ms for C922 MF OS timestamps in the same runs. SCR vs back-dated arrival: median +0.31 to +0.35 ms, robust sigma 46–66 µs. The xHCI IOCTL_USB_GET_FRAME_NUMBER_AND_QPC_FOR_TIME_SYNC mapping is exact only ~2–3.5 s after START_TRACKING; over 20 s it shifted +53/+117 µs (hc0) and −641 µs (hc1) and returned non-causal QPC in 41/396 and 208/396 samples, so the 30 s phase-2 agreement needs a re-check. C930e PTS is synthetic; use SCR/STC. Rolling shutter ~30 ms per frame, so time is per row. C930e only.

mjpeg.value: Yes: raw payload bytes; 0 corrupt in 2,135 strict decodes
mjpeg.note: Bytes come from reassembled isochronous payloads (uvc_frame_t.data), no decoder in the path. Strict (OpenCV/libjpeg-turbo) check: 2,135/2,135 across 6 verifier sweep runs. Not hash-compared against MF headers. The first frame after a zero-frame start was once truncated (no EOI, error bit set), so check EOI and the error bit.

unique_id.value: Port path + serial read without opening (libusb 1.0.30)
unique_id.note: The harness's --list reported port_path (e.g. 1-13.1.4) for every camera and the C922 serial B76395EF via libusb_get_device_string without opening (C922 still on usbvideo), plus Windows instance ID and location path. libusb port chains equal the Windows hub_port_chain for all 4 cameras (python-libusb1 check), so they map to the serial/port key in naming/camera_identity.py. USB addresses changed between enumerations; do not use them. Upstream libuvc's API exposes only bus/address/serial (SURVEY); the port path comes from libusb. Stability across reboot/port move untested.

bandwidth.value: App-forced alt: 720p30 at alt 5 (800 B), 1080p alt 8
bandwidth.note: Static scene, 20 s per alt, zero skipped frames. With full-contrast noise and focus pinned, 720p alt 6 was marginal (2 skips) and alt 7 clean; 1080p at alt 8 fell to 19.2 fps (alt 9 clean). Next to the generic camera (on MF) on the same hub the C930e streamed at alts 4–8 (alt 4 and 5 at ~30 fps in the retest); alt 9 was refused. Delivered fps followed 30/ceil(frame size/slot) in 47 of 48 runs. A refused start is followed by a zero-frame start. Only 2 cameras per link measured; '3–6 per link' is a model estimate. The generic camera has a single alt (3069 B).

exposure.value: Works only if re-applied after stream start (C930e)
exposure.note: uvc_set_ae_mode(1) + uvc_set_exposure_abs read back 78 (7.8 ms) in both cases, but with controls set only before COMMIT the flash step rise was ~32 ms (exposure scan peak ~38 ms); with --controls-after-start (AE/exposure/WB re-applied 0.5 s after start) it was ~12 ms, same as the C922. Reproduced by the verifier (vA vs vC). The only method in this group where an image-based check showed exposure taking effect. C922 and generic camera never tested on libusb.

format.value: MJPEG 480p/720p/1080p at 30 fps via PROBE/COMMIT
format.note: Width/height/fps negotiated with uvc_get_stream_ctrl_format_size; the harness hard-codes UVC_FRAME_FORMAT_MJPEG and only 30 fps was run. Other fps and uncompressed formats untested (expected: libuvc supports them).

focus.value: Autofocus off/on set and read back; absolute focus never set
focus.note: uvc_set_focus_auto rc 0 and auto_cur 1→0→1 on the C930e. Absolute focus read (85, range 0–255) but never set (set_abs_rc −999). Indirect image-side evidence: pinning AF removed the up-to-50% JPEG-size change between stream starts (agent report). Sharpness not checked. The only focus-control evidence in the whole libusb group.

rows.costs: WinUSB swap of the composite parent: admin, one UAC prompt, then a replug. The camera disappears from MF/DShow apps and its microphone vanishes. I wrote the ESP32 rig draft: the firmware compiles cleanly for `esp32:esp32:esp32`, and the host script parses and passes a synthetic self-test. Neither has been flashed or run on hardware, and nothing was measured.

**Files written** (only under `sync_rig/`; nothing else in the repo was touched):
- `C:/Users/Dom/GitHub/freemocap/skellycam/research/usb_cameras/sync_rig/esp32_sync_rig/esp32_sync_rig.ino`
- `C:/Users/Dom/GitHub/freemocap/skellycam/research/usb_cameras/sync_rig/host/esp32_clock_sync.py`
- `C:/Users/Dom/GitHub/freemocap/skellycam/research/usb_cameras/sync_rig/README.md`

**Compile result.** I used the existing arduino-cli 1.2.0 (`%LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs/Arduino IDE/.../arduino-cli.exe`) with the esp32:esp32 3.2.0 core (IDF v5.4) that was already installed. Nothing was installed or flashed. Build output went to the scratchpad, outside the repo.
- `compile --clean --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 --warnings all`: exit 0.
  - "Sketch uses 345778 bytes (26%) of program storage space. Maximum is 1310720 bytes."
  - "Global variables use 21156 bytes (6%) of dynamic memory, leaving 306524 bytes for local variables. Maximum is 327680 bytes."
  - The only warnings are 6 × `-Wmissing-field-initializers`, all from the IDF macro `MCPWM_GEN_COMPARE_EVENT_ACTION_END()`.
- Variant build with `-DCAP1_ROLE=1 -DUSE_RX_EDGE_CAPTURE=0`: exit 0, 345566 bytes.

**Python check:**
- `uv run --script ... --help`: exit 0.
- `python -m py_compile`: exit 0. I deleted the `__pycache__` it created.
- `--self-test` (synthetic pings, no serial port): pass.
  - Fitted drift 12.5088 ppm against a true 12.5.
  - Raw offset error −217.77 µs, which is inside the reported asymmetry bound of 397 µs.
  - Offset error after the reply-serialization correction: −0.757 µs.
  - Residual std 8.57 µs.

**Design deviations** (also listed in the README):
1. **Command syntax:** plain-word commands as the task specified (`MODE CODE`, `MODE STROBE p w ph [gap]`, `PING <host_ns>`, `STATUS`, and so on), not the design's `<STEP:us>` / `<PROTO:2>` framing. An optional `#tag` is echoed back, so protocol-2-style matching is still possible.
2. **Timer resolution:** all three PWM timers run at 2 MHz (0.5 µs), instead of 10 MHz for the latch and 1 MHz for the strobe, so they fit one group prescaler. The strobe and FSIN timers count up/down so a double pulse fits in one cycle. The cost is a maximum period of 65,535 µs.
3. **No `SWEEP` command.** For a slow phase sweep you set the strobe period directly; whole-µs periods give about 30 ppm steps.
4. **Timer alignment** uses a GPIO sync source on spare GPIO4, pulsed by software at START. IDF 5.x's software sync binds to only one timer, so it couldn't align all three.
5. **Reported timebase is `esp_timer_get_time()`**, as the task asked, not the capture timer the design wanted. Captured edges keep 12.5 ns resolution relative to each other, but their mapping to esp_timer has a fixed offset of about 1 µs or less; `STATUS` reports it as `anchor_half_ns`.
6. **GPIO34 watches either the latch or FSIN**, chosen at compile time (`CAP1_ROLE`), because wiring two outputs into one input would short them.
7. **Bar timing:** the bar pattern is rendered on the latch's falling edge, so the latch is closed before the next pattern shifts in. Strobe and FSIN phases are measured from the first latch edge after START.
8. **Output format:** event lines start with `EV` and carry ESP nanoseconds. PONG has a fourth token: `E` means the RX start bit was captured on GPIO39, `B` means it was estimated from when the line was read.
9. **Not written:** the `timing/rig/` analysis pipeline and event-log parser, the photodiode reading, the ESP32-S3 SOF lock, and DMA for the bar.

**Open TODOs:**
- **Unverified hardware behaviour.** These need a logic analyzer:
  - whether loading a timer on sync fires compare events;
  - the sync propagation delay;
  - how releasing a forced output behaves;
  - whether `mcpwm_timer_set_period` halves the period in up/down mode.
- **Render deadline at short steps.** At 50–100 µs steps the bar may miss its deadline; misses are reported as `EV E LATE`.
- **Clock anchor rejection.** The capture-timer anchor can pick up a serial RX edge's time if a byte arrives in the same microsecond. It should reject anchors whose residual jumps by more than a few µs.
- **Floating capture pins.** GPIO34, 35 and 39 need their loopback wires or 100 kΩ pull-downs.
- **Bar bit order** in the driver chain is unverified; the README has a walking-LED test for it.
- **Absolute clock offset is unresolved.** The host reports two offsets because it's unknown when the USB bridge forwards the reply. A ~50-byte reply takes ~0.54 ms to serialize at 921600 baud, so they differ by about 0.27 ms. Only the S3 SOF path can settle it.
- **Board reset on port open.** Some drivers still reset the DevKit when the port opens; a new `boot_id` means the clock fit restarts.
- **Next steps:** build the strobe-only P0 setup first, then port to the ESP32-S3 for the SOF lock.

# USB camera research: plan to fill the test gaps

Draft plan, 2026-10-30. Save as `research/usb_cameras/docs/test_gap_plan.md`. All paths are relative to `research/usb_cameras/` unless noted. Figures marked *est.* are estimates and nothing in this plan has been measured. Thresholds marked *proposed* need Dom's sign-off before any cell is rated with them.

---

## 1. Summary

**The decision this plan supports.** Which capture stack skellycam moves to:
- **Windows primary:** MF native MJPG with UVC metadata, as a C++ extension.
- **Windows fallback:** PyAV DirectShow `vcodec=mjpeg`.
- **Bandwidth path:** libusb on WinUSB, used only if more cameras per link matters enough to justify a driver swap.
- **Linux:** V4L2 or libusb.
- **macOS:** AVFoundation.
- **Hardware-trigger track:** FSIN, for G1.

Native MJPEG on Windows (G3) is already settled, and so is identity mapping through the MF and DirectShow paths (G4, apart from stability). What remains open is mostly the must-haves and the timing ground truth.

**The gaps that most affect the decision:**
1. **M3 focus has never been set on any capture path Dom would ship.** The usbvideo harnesses only read focus. The one focus write in the whole study was libuvc on WinUSB, on the C930e, with readback only. The C922's focus value moved between 0 and 40 across cells, so autofocus was running in every usbvideo test.
2. **M1 exposure has been shown to take effect in only one case:** libuvc with `--controls-after-start` on the C930e. Everywhere else the evidence is readback only. MF on the C930e applied it in 1 of 5 runs, and the C930e read back −5 on the DS side channel. Every libusb harness except libuvc's after-start mode sets exposure before COMMIT, the order that failed. No stack's own API (OpenCV `CAP_PROP_EXPOSURE`, PyAV, nokhwa) was tested.
3. **G1 has never been measured.** "No" is inferred, and phase walk is derived from 10–30 s rate figures. There is no ground truth without display scan-out, and no run longer than 30 s.
4. **G2 has a ~0.5 ms floor and no absolute latency.** The flash method cannot score below about 0.5 ms or give the absolute latency from light to timestamp. Only the MF and libusb sources were scored at all. The generic camera is unmeasured. The SCR→QPC basis holds for only about 2–3.5 s.
5. **G5 has been measured on the C930e only.** No link has carried three cameras, and the cost of a driver swap is not understood.
6. **G4 stability under reboot, replug and port move is untested,** as is an identical-camera pair.
7. **Nothing has run on Linux or macOS hardware.**

**The tests that close them, in priority order:**

| # | Test | Closes | Needs the rig? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C3** focus-control matrix (Siemens star) | M3 on every candidate | No |
| 2 | **C1** exposure-control matrix: set before vs after start, LogiTune on vs off. First pass on the existing flash step-response, then on the rig | M1, plus the C930e item (REPORT further investigation 6, PROGRESS §E) | Later |
| 3 | **R0/R1** ESP32 strobe rig, built and validated | Prerequisite for all S and T tests | n/a |
| 4 | **S1–S3** inter-camera exposure phase, ≥30 min drift, start alignment and topology | G1 for every free-running method | Yes |
| 5 | **T1–T4** every timestamp source scored against the rig (offset, causal, absolute); long SCR→QPC runs; C930e modes; generic camera | G2 | Yes |
| 6 | **B1–B3** WinUSB phase 3, three or more cameras per link, driver-swap strategy | G5 | No |
| 7 | **I1–I3** controlled reboot, replug and port move; identical pair; open-by-key on each API | G4 | No |
| 8 | **LX / MX** Linux and macOS sessions; **S4** FSIN spike when the OV9281s arrive | Off-Windows cells; G1 "yes" route | Partly |

**Why G1 needs few runs.** A free-running UVC camera's exposure phase belongs to the camera, not the API. So S1/S2 need running only once per camera pair, through MF. S3 then checks the one thing an API could change: start-time alignment. That fills the G1 column for every usbvideo and libusb row without a separate drift run for each method. Dom's assumption (no USB API aligns exposures) is the expected result. The plan measures it rather than assuming it, and S4 (FSIN) is the only test that could produce a G1 "yes".

## 3. Ground-truth upgrade

### 3.1 Choice of instrument

| Instrument | What it measures | Per-frame resolution | Rolling shutter | Host-clock link | Effort | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monitor flash (existing) | Offset-only timing of a source; relative exposure position | ~0.5 ms floor (measured, `timing/VERIFY_method.md`) | Mixed with display scan-out; GT offset moves 35 ms across image blocks | QPC (display) | Done | Baseline, and the cross-check in R1-V5 |
| **ESP32 strobe** (`sync_rig/`, P0) | s0 (row-0 exposure start), E, line time L, inter-camera phase | *est.* 10–20 µs | Measured: band edges give s0, E and L | Serial ping: *est.* 20–100 µs repeatability, with a bias bounded by about ±0.27 ms reply serialization (unresolved) | About $15 plus one bench evening | **Main instrument** for S, T and C1 |
| ESP32 LED bar (100 µs one-hot + Gray counter) | Exposure start and end at the bar's rows; coarse time | *est.* 15–30 µs | Bar laid along image rows | Same as the strobe | About $40 plus 1–2 evenings | Independent second method (R1-V4); sharpness side check for C3; global-shutter cameras (S4) |
| ESP32-S3 SOF lock (later) | ESP32 time ↔ USB frame number | *est.* ~1–10 µs to SOF | n/a | Removes the ping bias; chains to C930e SCR without QPC | About $15 plus firmware port | Absolute G2 latency at the tens-of-µs level; calibrates the ping path |
| Stock RocSync | Exposure start and end per frame, after the fact | 1 ms steps; paper reports 1.34 ms RMSE | Ring spans many rows, and the decoder assumes a global shutter | None | JLCPCB build from commit `5d82ddc` (HEAD firmware does not match the PCB) | **Not the bench instrument** |

**Where RocSync fits.**
- **Do not build it instead of the ESP32 rig.** Its 1 ms steps are coarser than the 0.5 ms floor we are trying to beat. The ring cannot cope with our ~30 ms rolling-shutter readout. It has no host link, so absolute latency cannot be scored, and it has no strobe or FSIN.
- **What to reuse:**
  - the one-hot "first and last lit LED" decoding, already adopted in the bar design;
  - the homography and `process_frame` structure (MPL-2.0, compatible with skellycam's AGPL).
- **Build it alongside only as a separate, later field-sync track,** for post-hoc ~1 ms alignment of heterogeneous cameras (GoPros, phones). That is a skellycam feature question, not a gap in this research.
- **Optional:** the bar firmware can add a 1 ms-step mode for the same field use.

**Truth reference for G2.** Report both:
- s0 (row-0 exposure start), and
- **t_light = mid-exposure of the image's centre row = s0 + (H/2)·L + E/2.** This is the closest single number to "when light hit the sensor" for a rolling-shutter frame.

## 4. Test specs

### Proposed rating thresholds

These map results to table cells. Dom to confirm.
- **G1** yes: exposure-start spread across cameras ≤ 0.1 ms (1σ), held ≥ 30 min without software correction. Partial: aligned at start but drifts, or a spread ≤ 1 ms. No: phase arbitrary or walking.
- **G2** yes: causal per-frame error ≤ 0.5 ms (1σ) against t_light, and absolute bias known to ±0.5 ms. Partial: ≤ 2 ms, or needs a per-camera calibration. No: arrival grid or synthetic.
- **M1** yes: measured E within max(0.1 ms, 5%) of the request in ≥ 99% of frames after the change takes effect; effect latency ≤ 5 frames; readback agrees; 3/3 runs on each camera. Partial: needs a workaround (for example re-apply after start), or works only on some cameras.
- **M2** yes: the requested mode is negotiated and read back, delivered fps is within 1% of the camera's real rate, and there is no silent fallback.
- **M3** yes: with AF off, static-scene sharpness varies by ≤ 2% (CV) over 120 s and there is no refocus after the target moves; manual focus steps change sharpness around a single peak; readback agrees.
- **G4** yes: the key survives reboot and same-port replug (and a port move for cameras with a serial), and the API opens exactly the camera with that key.
- **G5** yes: the app sets the alt or packet size, and N ≥ 3 cameras run at full rate on one USB 2.0 link with 0 strict-decode failures over 10 min.

### Rules for every test

- All camera access goes through `tools/camlock.py`.
- Kiyo stays unplugged or excluded.
- No programmatic device restarts; ask Dom to replug.
- Every UAC prompt is announced first.
- Results are JSON with the standard fields, in `results/windows/Gerald/<test>/` (or `results/linux/<host>/…`, `results/macos/<host>/…`).
- Reports are `.md` files under `research/`.
- Build outputs are never committed.

### G1: synchronisation

**S1. Inter-camera exposure phase (snapshot)**
- **Question:** what is the actual exposure-start phase between free-running cameras, measured without display scan-out?
- **Cameras:** C922, C930e and the generic, all via MF native (`timing/src/mf_uvc_timing.cpp`, one process per camera). The generic runs at 25.7 fps, so report its beat against the others, not a phase.
- **Hardware:** rig P0. The card fills the full image height of each camera, at 0.3–0.5 m. Dark room; AE, AWB and anti-flicker off.
- **Procedure:** strobe at 10 Hz with w = 50 µs, a 60 s run, repeated 5 times with a fresh stream start each time.
- **Analysis:** s0 per camera per strobe, then Δφ_AB = s0_A − s0_B (mod T).
- **Pass/decide:** this is a measurement. G1 "no" is confirmed if Δφ varies across starts and is not near 0.
- **Harness:** existing capture tool plus new `timing/rig/`. Unattended. No admin. *est.* 1 h.

**S2. Phase walk and drift, ≥ 30 min**
- **Question:** what are the relative rates (ppm) and the wander between camera pairs over time, and does any pair lock?
- **Setup:** as S1, with the strobe at 10 Hz for 60 min, 2 runs. Log CPU temperature or room temperature if available.
- **Analysis:**
  - linear fit of Δφ(t) giving relative ppm;
  - residual wander (Allan deviation);
  - comparison with the GT-derived +35 ppm (C930e) and −3.9 ppm (C922) rates (VERIFY_method §5).
- **Reuse:** this data also gives T1's long-run causal PTS→QPC mapping.
- **Harness:** existing plus `timing/rig/`. Unattended. *est.* 2.5 h machine time.

**S3. Start alignment and topology**
- **Question:** does simultaneous stream start narrow the phase on any API? Does sharing a hub or controller lock cameras to the USB SOF (0 ppm relative)?
- **Methods:**
  - MF: `bandwidth/build/mf_multi_open.exe --stagger-ms 0|2500 --arrivals --save-dir`;
  - PyAV dshow (threads released by a barrier; new small script);
  - libusb (`rust/uvc_iso` or libuvc) during the WinUSB window (B1).
- **Procedure:** 20 start/stop cycles for each of sequential, barrier and 2.5 s stagger. Topologies:
  - (a) same hub;
  - (b) different root ports on the same controller;
  - (c) different controllers (Gerald has two).
- **Analysis:**
  - Δφ distribution per start mode, with a KS test against uniform;
  - relative ppm per topology.
  - **Derived, no new run:** the useful life of a "restart until aligned" lottery, from S2's drift.
- **Pass/decide:** if every start mode gives a distribution consistent with uniform, the G1 cells stay "no" (measured). If any topology gives 0 ± 1 ppm, report "phase-stable but uncontrolled" (partial at most).
- **Harness:** mostly existing; a barrier script for PyAV is new. Unattended, but needs Dom to move cables for topology (b)/(c), *est.* 10 min. *est.* 3 h machine time.

**S4. FSIN hardware-trigger spike**
- **Question:** does a shared FSIN edge align exposures, and how tightly? This is the only test that can produce G1 "yes".
- **Hardware:**
  - ≥ 2 (ideally 4) InnoMaker U20CAM-9281M;
  - rig with FSIN outputs: AO3400A or ULN2803A sinks to the opto inputs (+5 V, about 19 mA each);
  - LED bar, or strobe-phase sweep (global shutter; see §3.3).
- **Procedure** (replaces the swept-flash part of `../arduino_sync/PLAN.md` M0):
  - FSIN at 20.8 ms (48.08 Hz);
  - sweep strobe delay d = 0–25 ms in 50 µs steps, for an exposure-window map per camera;
  - lockout sweep with FSIN period 16–30 ms;
  - the remaining M0 items (same-handle DSHOW `CT_FOCUS_AUTO` trigger write, pulse-removal check, buffers).
  - Note whether the OV9281 board has autofocus (M3 applicability; *expected:* fixed lens).
- **Analysis:** FSIN→exposure skew per camera, its spread across cameras, frame-to-frame jitter, and lockout as a function of fps, exposure and resolution.
- **Pass (*proposed*):** skew spread ≤ 100 µs and jitter ≤ 50 µs gives G1 "yes" for the FSIN row. Otherwise partial, with the numbers.
- **Harness:** the rig's FSIN timer exists in the draft. Capture code is new (planned in arduino_sync M0). Attended wiring, *est.* 2–3 h of Dom's time. *est.* 1 day total.

**S5 (optional). UVC still-image trigger**
- **Why only one camera:** the descriptors (`results/windows/Gerald/naming_rerun_20261027/win_identity_dump/descriptors.json`) show `bStillCaptureMethod=2` and `bTriggerSupport=1` only on the generic 4C4A:4A55. The C922 and C930e are 0/0.
- **Question:** does a still trigger start an exposure, or just pick the next frame?
- **Procedure:** DS `IAMVideoControl::SetMode(VideoControlFlag_Trigger)` on the still pin, under usbvideo with no driver swap. 50 triggers while the rig strobes. Measure the latency from trigger write to the still frame's s0.
- **Expected:** latency uniform over 0–T (free-running sensor), so no.
- **Harness:** new. Unattended. *est.* 2 h. Run it only if time allows.
- **Vendor XUs:** out of scope. None is documented as a trigger, and blind writes risk leaving the device in a bad state.

# USB camera research: plan to fill the test gaps

Revised draft plan, 2026-10-30. Save it as `research/usb_cameras/docs/test_gap_plan.md`. Paths are relative to `research/usb_cameras/` unless noted.

- Figures marked *est.* are estimates. Nothing in this plan has been measured yet.
- Thresholds marked *proposed* need Dom's sign-off before any cell is rated with them.
- Claims taken from outside the repo are marked *web*, with the source.

---

## 1. Summary

**The decision this plan supports** is which capture stack skellycam moves to:
- **Windows primary:** MF native MJPG with UVC metadata, as a C++ extension.
- **Windows fallback:** PyAV DirectShow `vcodec=mjpeg`.
- **Bandwidth path:** libusb on WinUSB. Use it only if fitting more cameras per link is worth a driver swap.
- **Linux:** V4L2 or libusb.
- **macOS:** AVFoundation.
- **Hardware-trigger track:** FSIN, for G1.

**Already settled on Windows:**
- G3: native MJPEG.
- G4: identity mapping through the MF and DirectShow paths. Stability is still open.

Most of what remains open is the must-haves and the timing ground truth.

**The gaps that most affect the decision:**
1. **M3: focus has never been set on any path Dom would ship.**
   - The usbvideo harnesses only read focus.
   - The only focus write in the whole study was libuvc on WinUSB, on the C930e, and it was checked by readback only.
   - The C922's focus value moved between 0 and 40 across cells, so autofocus was running in every usbvideo test.
2. **M1: exposure has been shown to take effect in only one case:** libuvc with `--controls-after-start` on the C930e. Everywhere else the evidence is readback only.
   - MF on the C930e applied it in 1 of 5 runs.
   - The C930e accepts nothing below −5 through the DS side channel.
   - Every libusb harness except libuvc's after-start mode sets exposure before COMMIT, which is the order that failed.
   - In the MJPEG matrix, exposure was set through the DS filter even in MF cells, so MF's own exposure path is not demonstrated.
   - No stack's own API was tested (OpenCV `CAP_PROP_EXPOSURE`, PyAV, nokhwa).
3. **G1 has never been measured.**
   - "No" is inferred.
   - There is no ground truth without display scan-out, and no run was longer than 30 s.
   - **The study holds two phase-walk figures that contradict each other:**
     - About one frame every 20–25 s. This comes from 10 s delivered-fps differences (30.00 vs 30.04 fps ≈ 1300 ppm). It is almost certainly an artefact of counting or of the 16 ms grid.
     - About one frame every ~14 min. This comes from the PTS-vs-ground-truth rates (+35 ppm for the C930e, −3.9 ppm for the C922, about 39 ppm relative; `timing/VERIFY_method.md` §5).
   - **Until S2 runs, the README may cite only the ppm-derived walk, labelled *derived*.** It must not cite the fps-derived figure.
4. **G2 has a floor of about 0.5 ms and no absolute latency.**
   - The flash method cannot score below about 0.5 ms and cannot give the absolute latency from light to timestamp.
   - Only the MF and libusb sources were scored.
   - The generic camera has not been measured.
   - The SCR→QPC basis holds for only about 2–3.5 s.
   - Nobody has checked whether a DS/KS client can read UVC PTS/SCR at all (`docs/capture_backends_review.md`). That decides whether the PyAV DS fallback can ever do better than G2 "no".
5. **G5 has been measured on the C930e only.**
   - No link has carried three cameras.
   - The cost of a driver swap is not understood.
6. **G4 stability under reboot, replug and port move is untested,** and so is a pair of identical cameras.
7. **MF's Frame Server CPU cost is unmeasured.** It needs elevation (PROGRESS: "Still needs a human"). It bears directly on choosing MF over PyAV DS.
8. **Nothing has run on Linux or macOS hardware.**

**The tests that close them, in priority order:**

| # | Test | Closes | Needs the rig? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C3** focus-control matrix (Siemens star; exposure, gain and WB locked) | M3 on every candidate | No |
| 2 | **C1** exposure-control matrix. Per-camera in-range set points; set before vs after start; LogiTune on vs off. The pre-rig pass can rate only "no" or "partial (pending rig)" | M1, plus the C930e item (REPORT further investigation 6, PROGRESS §E) | For "yes" |
| 3 | **R0/R1** ESP32 strobe rig built and validated (V0–V6); later **R2** ESP32-S3 SOF lock (V7) | Prerequisite for every S and T test, and for absolute G2 | n/a |
| 4 | **S1–S3** exposure phase between cameras, ≥ 30 min drift, start alignment and topology; **S6 (opt)** closed-loop steering | G1 for every free-running method | Yes |
| 5 | **T1–T5** every timestamp source scored against the rig; long SCR→QPC runs; C930e modes; generic camera; DS metadata probe | G2 | Yes (T5 feasibility: no) |
| 6 | **X2** Frame Server CPU (elevated) | MF vs PyAV DS choice | No |
| 7 | **B1–B4** WinUSB phase 3, three or more cameras per link, driver-swap strategy, integrity | G5 | No |
| 8 | **I1–I3** controlled reboot, replug and port move; identical pair; open-by-key on each API | G4 | No |
| 9 | **LX / MX** Linux and macOS sessions; **S4** FSIN spike when the OV9281s arrive | Off-Windows cells; the G1 "yes" route | Partly |

**How G1 is rated, and why it needs few runs.**
- A free-running UVC camera's exposure phase belongs to the camera, not to the API. So S1 and S2 run once per camera pair, through MF.
- S3 then tests the one thing an API could change, start-time alignment, on three paths:
  - MF;
  - PyAV DS;
  - libuvc (the one libusb path).
- Only those three rows get **measured** G1 cells. Every other usbvideo and libusb row is rated **"n·i (transferred from S1–S3 on MF)"**, and the plan does not present those as measured.
- G1 is rated by **controllability**, not by a snapshot. Two free-running cameras that happen to land ≤ 1 ms apart in one run are still "no".
- Every cell keeps two things apart:
  - **measures the offset** (G2: the method can timestamp exposure);
  - **aligns the exposure** (G1: the method can move it).
- Dom's assumption (no USB API aligns exposures) is the expected result, and the plan measures it rather than assuming it.
- Routes to G1:
  - S4 (FSIN) is the only open-loop route to "yes".
  - S6 (software phase steering) can reach "partial" at most.

---

## 2. Gap table

**Cell format:** `rating·basis → test`.
- **Rating:** y = yes, p = partial, n = no, ? = unknown, n/a.
- **Basis:** m = measured, i = inferred, w = web, nt = not tested.
- **Markers:**
  - `done`: no test is needed.
  - `out`: out of scope, with the reason in the Note column.
  - `(opt)`: run only if that method is still a candidate.
  - `n·i (tr)`: G1 transferred from S1–S3 on MF, not measured on that path.

| Method | G1 sync | G2 timestamp | G3 MJPEG | G4 ID | G5 bandwidth | M1 exposure | M2 format | M3 focus | Note |

### 3.3 R1: validate the rig before using it

**Strobe timing for every camera run.** Never use an exact submultiple of the frame period. A 10 Hz strobe is exactly 1/3 of 30.00 fps, so the band would park on fixed rows.
- Use period = T_cam + 33 µs. This follows `sync_rig/README.md` deviation 4: integer µs, about 30 ppm granularity.
- Per-frame band runs use about 33,366 µs. Sparse runs use 3·T_cam + 33 µs.
- The band then walks every row in about 33 s.
- Rows the band never appears on are flagged as vertical blanking, and strobes that land there are dropped, not scored.
- The 25.7 fps generic camera beats against any strobe period, so it is handled the same way.

**Global-shutter caveat** (needed for S4). A global-shutter sensor such as the OV9281 produces no row band: a frame is either lit or not. For those cameras, use the strobe-phase sweep (FSIN edge + d, with d swept in 50 µs steps) or the LED bar.

**New analysis code** goes in `timing/rig/`, following §F of the rig design:
- event-log parser;
- clock correlation;
- tone-curve calibration from a strobe-width sweep;
- band detector with a blanking-gap map;
- band-to-strobe assignment;
- per-frame solve;
- bar decoder;
- scorers.

It also needs adapters that read each harness's `frames.jsonl` and session JSON.

**Truth reference for G2.** Report both:
- **s0**, the row-0 exposure start;
- **t_light**, the mid-exposure of the image's centre row: t_light = s0 + (H/2)·L + E/2.

t_light is the closest single number to "when light hit the sensor" for a rolling-shutter frame, where the readout takes about 30 ms per frame.

## 4. Test specs

### Proposed rating thresholds

These map results to table cells. Dom to confirm.

**G1 (rated by controllability, never by a single-run snapshot)**
- **Yes:** the method aligns exposure start across cameras to ≤ 0.1 ms (1σ) **on every start, open loop**, and holds it ≥ 30 min without software correction.
- **Partial:** the method reproduces an alignment within a stated spread (≤ 1 ms) **on demand**, by any of:
  - ≥ 18/20 starts within that spread;
  - a start-mode Δφ distribution in S3 that rejects uniform and is concentrated within that spread;
  - a closed-loop method (S6) that holds the spread for a stated time. Software steering is capped at "partial (software steering, needs a ground-truth reference)".
- **No:** the phase is arbitrary across starts (Δφ consistent with uniform), **whatever a single run's spread happens to be**. A pair that is phase-stable but not controllable is "no", with a note.
- **Wording:** cells say "aligns exposure" (G1) or "measures offset" (G2), and never mix the two.

**G2**
- **Yes:** causal per-frame error ≤ 0.5 ms (1σ) against t_light, **and** an absolute bias known to ±0.5 ms. Absolute requires V7; until then, see V6.
- **Partial:** ≤ 2 ms, or needs a per-camera calibration, or the absolute bias is only estimated.
- **No:** an arrival grid or a synthetic timestamp.

**M1** (rated per camera × path)
- **Yes:** all of:
  - measured E (rig) is within max(0.1 ms, 5%) of the request in ≥ 99% of frames after the change takes effect;
  - the change takes effect within ≤ 5 frames;
  - readback agrees;
  - 3/3 runs on each camera.
- **Partial:** needs a workaround (for example re-applying after start), or works only on some cameras.
- Clamping of an out-of-range request is recorded as **clamp behaviour**, not as "not applied".

**M2**
- **Yes:** all of:
  - the requested mode is negotiated and read back;
  - the delivered frame dimensions match the request (from JPEG SOF0, or the decoded shape);
  - delivered fps is within 1% of the **camera's real rate**, defined as that camera's rate on MF native in the same mode;
  - there is no silent fallback.
- A camera that cannot reach the requested fps on any path is reported as a camera limitation, not a method failure.

**M3**
- **Yes:** all of:
  - with AF off and exposure, gain and WB locked, static-scene sharpness varies by ≤ 2% (CV) over 120 s;
  - no refocus after the target moves;
  - manual focus steps change sharpness around a single peak;
  - readback agrees.

**G4**
- **Yes:** the key survives a reboot and a same-port replug (plus a port move, for cameras with a serial), and the API opens exactly the camera with that key.

**G5**
- **Yes:** the app sets the alt setting or packet size, **and** N ≥ 3 cameras run at full rate on one USB 2.0 link for 10 min, **and** each camera's strict-decode failure rate is no worse than its own usbvideo baseline in the same mode. The generic camera's 1080p strict-decode failures are camera behaviour on every API.

### G1: synchronisation

**S1. Exposure phase between cameras (snapshot across starts)**
- **Question:** what is the exposure-start phase between free-running cameras, measured without display scan-out, and does it change from one start to the next?
- **Cameras:**
  - C922, C930e and the generic, via MF native (`timing/src/mf_uvc_timing.cpp`, one process per camera);
  - rig-run topology, with the 10 s pre-check;
  - the generic camera runs at 25.7 fps, so report its beat against the others, not a phase.
- **Hardware:**
  - rig P0, after V0–V5 have passed;
  - the card fills the full image height of each camera, at 0.3–0.5 m;
  - dark room; AE, AWB and anti-flicker off;
  - exposures from the per-camera set points.
- **Procedure:**
  - detuned strobe (T_cam + 33 µs), w = 50 µs;
  - 60 s run, repeated 5 times with a fresh stream start each time.
- **Analysis:** s0 per camera per strobe, then Δφ_AB = s0_A − s0_B (mod T), for each start.
- **Rating input:** this feeds the G1 controllability rating together with S3. A small Δφ in one run proves nothing.
- **Harness:** the existing capture tool plus the new `timing/rig/`. Unattended after setup, no admin. *est.* 1 h.

**S2. Phase walk and drift, ≥ 30 min**
- **Question:** what are the relative rates and the wander between camera pairs, and does any pair lock?
- **Setup:** as in S1, with a 60 min sparse detuned strobe, 2 runs. Log CPU temperature or room temperature if available. Check disk space first.
- **Analysis:**
  - linear fit of Δφ(t), giving **relative ppm for each pair**;
  - residual wander (Allan deviation).
- **Report explicitly which prior figure S2 confirms:**
  - the ppm-derived walk (+35 / −3.9 ppm, about one frame per ~14 min), or
  - the 10 s fps-derived "frame every ~20–25 s".
- After S2, only S2's measured walk goes in the README.
- **Reuse:** this data also gives T1's long-run causal PTS→QPC mapping.
- **Harness:** existing plus `timing/rig/`. Unattended. *est.* 2.5 h machine time.

**S3. Start alignment and topology**
- **Question:** does a simultaneous stream start narrow the phase on any API? Does sharing a hub or controller lock cameras to the USB SOF (0 ppm relative)?
- **Methods.** These are the only paths whose G1 cells become measured; every other row is transferred.
  - MF: `bandwidth/build/mf_multi_open.exe --stagger-ms 0|2500 --arrivals --save-dir`.
  - PyAV dshow: threads released by a barrier; new small script.
  - libuvc (patch 0001) during the WinUSB window (B1).
- **Procedure:** 20 start/stop cycles for each start mode (sequential, barrier, 2.5 s stagger), on each topology:
  - (a) same hub: **two cameras only, C922 + C930e**, on usbvideo (and libuvc in D2);
  - (b) different root ports on the same controller: three cameras, if the 10 s pre-check passes;
  - (c) different controllers (Gerald has two): three cameras.
  - Record the topology with `win_usb_topology.py --pipes-only` for each.
- **Analysis:**
  - Δφ distribution per start mode, with a KS test against uniform, and the count of starts within ±1 ms and ±0.1 ms;
  - relative ppm per topology.
  - **Derived, no new run:** how long a "restart until aligned" lottery stays useful, from S2's drift.
- **Decision:**
  - Uniform in every start mode: G1 "no (measured)" for MF, PyAV DS and libuvc.
  - A concentrated distribution meeting the G1 "partial" rule: "partial".
  - Any topology at 0 ± 1 ppm: report "phase-stable but uncontrolled", which is still "no" unless the start phase is also controllable.
- **Harness:** mostly existing; the PyAV barrier script is new. Unattended, but Dom moves cables for (a)/(b)/(c), *est.* 10 min. *est.* 3 h machine time.

**S4. FSIN hardware-trigger spike**
- **Question:** does a shared FSIN edge align exposures, and how tightly? This is the only open-loop test that can produce G1 "yes".
- **Hardware:**
  - ≥ 2 (ideally 4) InnoMaker U20CAM-9281M;
  - rig FSIN outputs: AO3400A or ULN2803A sinks to the opto inputs (+5 V, about 19 mA each);

  - FSIN at 20.8 ms (48.08 Hz).
  - Sweep the strobe delay d from 0 to 25 ms in 50 µs steps, to map each camera's exposure window.
  - Lockout sweep with the FSIN period from 16 to 30 ms.
  - **Exposure under trigger (M1):** set manual exposure at two values. The swept window width must change by the expected amount. Record readback.
  - **Format under trigger (M2):**
    - resolution and pixel format stay as negotiated (SOF0 check);
    - delivered fps equals the pulse rate;
    - record readback of the negotiated type.
  - The remaining M0 items: the same-handle DSHOW `CT_FOCUS_AUTO` trigger write, the pulse-removal check, and buffers.
  - Note whether the OV9281 board has autofocus. This decides whether M3 applies. *expected:* fixed lens.
- **Analysis:**
  - FSIN→exposure skew per camera, and its spread across cameras;
  - frame-to-frame jitter;
  - lockout as a function of fps, exposure and resolution.
- **Pass (*proposed*):** skew spread ≤ 100 µs and jitter ≤ 50 µs give G1 "yes" for the FSIN row. Otherwise "partial", with the numbers.
- **Harness:**
  - the rig's FSIN timer exists in the draft;
  - the capture code is new (planned in arduino_sync M0).
- **Time:** attended wiring, *est.* 2–3 h of Dom's time; *est.* 1 day total.

**S6 (optional). Closed-loop software phase steering**
- **Question:** can a USB-only app *steer* exposure phase without FSIN?
- **Cameras:** C922 + C930e, with the rig running as the reference.

  - C930e DS: −5, −4, −3;

- **Target:** an A4 Siemens star on matte paper at about 1 m.

**Ordering notes:**
- **Rig before WinUSB.** D3a mounts and validates the rig on Gerald and stops the LogiTune updater **before** D2. Two reasons:
  - the libusb legs in D2 are scored on the rig;
  - the stopped updater (and quitting the agent and Razer) is a prerequisite for the WinUSB install. Without it, a vetoed restart leaves DN_NEED_RESTART.
- **WinUSB before the long MF runs.** The rollback creates new instance IDs that need the metadata registry value set again. Doing D2 first means that UAC prompt and replug happen once (UAC #5), and the same prompt covers T4's generic camera.
- **LogiTune order.** The updater stays stopped from UAC #1 through D2 and through the "off" legs in D3b. It is restored (UAC #6) only once those are done, and the "on" legs of T3b, C1 and C3 run last.
- **Phase walk in the README.** Until S2 has run, step 10 (and any interim README edit) cites only the ppm-derived phase walk (about one frame per ~14 min, labelled *derived*). It never cites the 10 s fps-derived "frame every ~20–25 s".
- **Must-haves first.** C3 and the pre-rig C1 pass come first on purpose. They need no new hardware and give early evidence on the two must-haves that most affect the stack choice. M1 "yes" still waits for the rig pass.
